title: Section-one normalization of compact cohomology of a closed rational point
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], put $S=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, and let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Let $q:Y\to S$ be proper with $Y$ Noetherian, meaning that it admits a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion and $i:S\hookrightarrow U$ a closed immersion such that $k=ji:S\hookrightarrow Y$ is closed and $qk=\mathrm{id}_S$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use constant-$A$ module sheaves on small etale sites and ordinary derived categories [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Set $F=k_*A_S$, $G=i_*A_S$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Identify $j^{-1}F=G$ by the restriction isomorphism acting identically on sections over the corresponding fibre products [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Let $e:j_!G\to F$ be the actual counit of the extension-by-zero adjunction $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] at $F$, under this identification [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], and assume that $e$ is an isomorphism.

Use the chosen compactification $(j,q)$ of $f=qj$ for compact supports [def-amb-etale-compact-support], so $R\Gamma_c(U,G)=R\Gamma(Y,j_!G)$. There is a canonical isomorphism in the derived category of $A$-modules
$$\beta:R\Gamma(Y,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}A[0],$$
whose degree-zero map is $\Gamma(Y,k_*A_S)=\Gamma(S,A_S)=A$, acting as the identity on the section $1$. Let $u:A_Y\to F$ be the inverse-image/direct-image unit for $k$, let $\eta:A[0]\to R\Gamma(Y,A_Y)$ be the constant-section map, and define
$$\lambda=(\beta\circ R\Gamma(e))^{-1}:A[0]\longrightarrow R\Gamma_c(U,G).$$
Then the specified derived maps obey
$$\beta\circ R\Gamma(u)\circ\eta=\mathrm{id}_{A[0]},\qquad R\Gamma(e)\circ\lambda=R\Gamma(u)\circ\eta.$$
In particular $\lambda$ is the inverse of the compact-source identification normalized by section $1$, with no scalar rescaling.

proof.text: The derived-composition comparison identifies the composite of the Γ_Y derived unit on F(K) and RΓ_Y applied to the F derived unit on K with the derived unit of F⋙Γ_Y, up to the canonical homotopy-composition isomorphism. Exactness of F and F⋙Γ_Y makes the latter two units invertible. Cancellation proves that the Γ_Y unit on F(K) is invertible. Apply this to the single complex A_S[0] and transport through singleMapHomologicalComplex. Every other factor in sectionsAugmentation is an isomorphism. Together with the constant-section unit this makes pointSection invertible.

proof.text: For every étale Y-object W, the canonical comparison Γ(Y,k_*G)→Γ(S,G) followed by restriction to W×_Y S equals restriction of Γ(Y,k_*G) to W. This follows by expanding the comparison through terminal-object evaluation: the two maps from W×_Y S to the pulled-back terminal object coincide by terminal uniqueness. Evaluate the closedUnit map at W=id_Y. The unit compatibility of leftAdjointUniq defining constantSheafCompUpperStarIso identifies its composite with constant sections with the constant-section unit on S. Transporting along the Γ/evaluation comparisons gives η_Y≫Γ_Y(closedUnit)=η_S≫comparison.inv. Naturality of sectionsAugmentation then proves unitSection=pointSection directly in D(A).

proof.text: Define β to be the inverse of pointSection. Its section normalization is hom_inv_id, and unitSection=pointSection proves the second equation. The derived counit is invertible by the assumed invertibility of the actual counit; cancellation proves the specified inverse-composite equation. Any other normalized β has the same hom after precomposition with the invertible pointSection, hence equals β.
